verdicts.reason: Both scramble the benefit list (1, then 4, 3, 2), wedge the 'Find Solstice' line between bullets, misalign the bullet indents, and move the CTA above the headline. A at least keeps the headline near the top, though its bullets run over the green circle and the can sits isolated low on the page. B puts the headline under the product, blows the logo pill up to dominate the footer, and crams the legal text into a narrow ragged column.

Both have the same layout, with the list order scrambled, the body copy jammed between bullets, the CTA above the headline and ragged bullet indents. A's huge logo pill overpowers the footer and its legal copy wraps into a cramped five-line column. B keeps the logo pill proportionate, sets the legal text in a sensible two-line block and has slightly larger, more legible type.

A shrinks the CTA to an illegible sliver and the logo to a near-invisible pill at the very bottom, leaves a large dead gap between the can and the footer, and orphans 'grocer.' on its own line. B keeps the CTA and logo readable but still scrambles the list order, inserts body copy between bullets, runs the bullets over the circle and puts the CTA above the headline.

B's CTA is too small to read and its logo is nearly invisible at the bottom; it also has a big empty gap above the footer and orphans 'grocer.' on its own line. A keeps the CTA, logo and legal text legible and proportionate, but still scrambles the list order, splits the bullets with body copy and puts the CTA above the headline and product.
